basis: Reviewed revision 4 exact spec, full Lean model, all 22 registered SQL propositions and real revision 3 backup failure evidence. Native SQL PREPARE/EXECUTE have an explicit exact-source admission and connection-local shared namespace design; no backup content downgrade or parser bypass is proposed.

The six new propositions establish conditional abstract provenance, rejection of unknown names, native-prepare-to-bind reachability, pure cache lookup, and positive witnesses. bodyPart proves only a nonempty exact substring; semantic body classification and source-span extraction are trusted adapter obligations.

SQLean statementFamilies derives outer grammar productions, which can present ExecuteStmt for CREATE TABLE AS EXECUTE; singleton ordered families alone therefore do not establish that EXECUTE is top-level. Spec requires sole top-level statements, so enforce both first real token PREPARE/EXECUTE and the singleton ordered family in the implementation, alongside production-based restrictions.
implementation_acceptance_notes: Apply nested opaque, mode, function and resource restrictions across whole PREPARE and EXECUTE expressions. Reject nested, multiple-statement, quoted, Unicode-escaped and overlong name cases; normalize only unquoted ASCII SQL names, while protocol names remain exact.

Use one connection-local accepted-provenance table for SQL and wire protocol, including pipelining, Bind capture, duplicate/failing preparation and server-error transitions. Admission is not proof of backend success; no cache hit creates state. Tests must cover both cross-protocol directions and colliding names.

Preserve and replay the full pg_dump/pg_restore path including ACLs and the prior failure evidence. Re-run finite protocol, recovery and application acceptance without weakening grammar or backup contents.
Perform the two planned clean proof builds against the exact revision 4 and model hashes before implementation. I did not independently run Lean or runtime tests for this review.
formal_limits: Lean is an abstract model of accepted provenance, not a proof of parser report classification, name normalization, SQL body span, wire implementation or PostgreSQL execution. bodyPart does not show that its substring is the actual parsed body.
Optimistically tracking an admitted request is not a claim that PostgreSQL created or executed a statement; server errors and stale names need conservative runtime handling.
approval_scope: Exact revision 4 bounded design only, conditional on final clean proof and separate runtime/recovery checks.
